title: Poppy Seed, Lemon and Sunflower Seed Pancakes
changes_from_base: A wholemeal buttermilk batter with poppy seeds, toasted sunflower seeds and lemon zest, oil instead of melted butter and no soured cream, with raspberries pressed onto each pancake if you like.
summary: Hearty wholemeal pancakes studded with poppy and sunflower seeds and bright lemon zest, with raspberries pressed in for bursts of fruit.

ingredients.item: wholemeal flour (or 140 g wholemeal plus 140 g plain flour)
fine sea salt or table salt
butter or oil, for the pan

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Sift the 280 g wholemeal flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda, 1 tbsp sugar and ½ tsp salt together, then stir in the 25 g poppy seeds and 45 g toasted sunflower seeds.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the 2 eggs, then whisk in the 480 ml buttermilk, 2 tbsp rapeseed oil and 2 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Quickly stir the flour mix and 2 tbsp lemon zest into the wet ingredients, taking care not to overwork the batter.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat a griddle over medium-high heat and brush with butter or oil.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drop 3-4 tbsp batter per pancake, pressing about 6 raspberries onto each if using.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: When bubbles break through the surface, flip and cook for about 1 min more until brown underneath.

tips: Toast the sunflower seeds until golden first for extra crunch and flavour.
Stir the batter just until combined - overmixing makes the pancakes tough.
Press the raspberries in as soon as the batter is on the griddle so they set into the pancakes.
storage: Serve straight away, or once cool, wrap portions in cling film and freeze in a freezer bag. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
